## Our Commitment to Environmental Management

#### **ICMM** principles:

Environmental Performance Conservation of Biodiversity

Responsible Production

We express our commitment to environmental management through a declaration to achieve Net Zero Emission in scopes 1 and 2 by 2050, in line with the Paris Agreement. The nickel plant we operate in Sorowako has a carbon intensity of 29.50 Ton CO2eq/Ton Ni, making PT Vale the company with the lowest carbon intensity in Indonesia. In addition, PT Vale started testing electric cars and trucks in Sorowako on January 14 and August 4, 2022.

PT Vale has been progressively reclaiming post-mining land, targeting the reclamation of 70% of the total area by 2025, and rehabilitating watersheds. The area of land rehabilitated until the end of 2022 is 10,280 hectares, comprising 10,000 hectares outside the operational area and 295.5 hectares within the operational area. We also planted 3.7 million trees, including endemic species.

## **Our Commitment to Community Development (Social)**
**ICMM principles:**  Human Rights Social Performances Stakeholder Engagement Health and Safety

Since its establishment, PT Vale has been committed to benefitting community members in its working areas. The company has contracted 11,000 local people, either as employees or suppliers/partners, 87% of which come from East Luwu Regency and other areas in South Sulawesi.

To improve the quality of our human resources, we facilitated several of our employees to take an engineering study program at various universities, including the University of Hasanuddin. In addition, PT Vale facilitated and encouraged the relevant employees to get a professional engineering certificate and an engineering registration certificate from the Indonesian Engineer Association. PT Vale also established the Academy Teknik Sorowako (Sorowako Technical Academy), from which 1,516 people have graduated.

We contributed 44% to the Gross Regional Domestic Product of East Luwu Regency, the largest in the mining sector. Our support for the local economy can also be seen from the transfer of the Sorowako Airport to the provincial government of South Sulawesi through the signing of a deed releasing the Sorowako Airport between the President Director of PT Vale Indonesian Tbk and the Governor of South Sulawesi on May 12, 2022. Sorowako Airport management by the provincial government is expected to support tourism and agribusiness in East Luwu and South Sulawesi in general.

## **CEO Message** [POJK51-D.1][2-22a]
Febriany Eddy CEO and President Director

*"We hope that the support provided will continue, and the cooperation that has been built will get even better to lead PT Vale to realize its ambition to become a pioneer of sustainable mining practices in Indonesia and even the world."*

The current global dynamics emphasize environmental and social aspects to mitigate risks and support sustainable economic performance. Taking on our commitment to embed a culture of sustainability, we constantly improve our best sustainability practices. Entering 2022, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk, as part of Vale S.A., began to adopt sustainable mine management principles based on the International Council of Mining and Metals (ICMM) Sustainable Development Framework.

We carry out every company activity by referring to the Sustainable Mine Management Principles and ensure related parties' activities comply with the same principles and initiative. By complying with the principles and initiative, we seek to ensure that our mineral (nickel) products are the results of responsible production processes. In this way, we can continue to meet demands for sustainable nickel, support global economic decarbonization, and contribute to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The Company's efforts to be sustainable in 2022 faced formidable challenges, including stakeholders' different perceptions about and interests in their sustainability performance delivery. Another challenge was the limitation that the Company had in applying all methods of calculation and documentation to manage the negative impact of operations. Two solutions we were continuously working on were improving communications and training and monitoring calculation data recording to be the basis for performance evaluation. Another challenge we faced was the Furnace#4 Rebuild, leading to a decrease in the production number compared to the previous year.

We recorded positive achievements in environmental, social, governance, and economic management in 2022. Overall, the total GHG emissions up to 2022 have cumulatively decreased by 60,422 tons of CO2 eq, from the 2017 baseline of 2,013,950 tons of CO2 eq. This achievement is still in the projected net zero emission roadmap which will be gradually implemented at PT Vale. However, we also recorded that there are fluctuations in the volume of GHG emissions every year, influenced by the proportion of fuel used in operations and the amount of production. We rehabilitated transboundary land and forests outside our mining operation areas in 13 South Sulawesi districts

and three West Java districts. During our operations for more than 50 years, we have protected Lakes Matano, Mahalona, and Towuti from pollution resulting from the impacts of our mining operations and our nickel in matte production.

The same is true for our health sustainability performance. While fostering employment relations, we keep promoting to increase employee awareness about gender equality and diversity following our Diversity and Inclusion Charter. In occupational health and safety (OHS), PT Vale implements the Mineral and Coal Mining Safety System (SMKP Minerba) and has audited our compliance with the mining safety system and IMS–Environment Health and Safety Management System, with a compliance rate of 70.24% in 2022 as a result, lower than that in 2021, which was 75.18%. However, we also note that we should have managed our OHS performance better because there was a fatal incident involving a contractor or work partner in this reporting period. This incident left deep sorrow for PT Vale, as for us safety is everything. As a followup, PT Vale has implemented a complete safety stand down for all lines of operations. Besides, PT Vale has also cooperated with the international consultant to investigate the case and has improved occupational safety in all workshops involving tires.

We manage our social impacts by building synergy with the local governments and contributing to regional economic development. In 2022, PT Vale still implemented the Integrated Community Empowerment and Development Program (PPM) covering the Sorowako, Bahodopi, and Pomalaa Blocks with the funding support of US\$6,381,165. PT Vale transferred the Sorowako Airport to the provincial

government of South Sulawesi in this reporting period. The airport is now a public airport under the provincial government's management. It is expected to support tourism in the province, particularly in East Luwu. We continuously opened dialogues with the local communities native to our operational areas to find the best solution to some differences that were our shared concerns. Our sincerity in managing our social impacts earned support from the communities, local governments, and other stakeholders, leading to the Company's smooth activities without significant upheavals in 2022.

We put sustainable governance into practice to support our sustainable operations, which in turn will increase stakeholders' trust. We place importance on legal compliance based on business ethics, prompting us to take our actions responsibly, honestly, confidently, respectfully, and loyally. As a form of compliance, PT Vale implemented several activities in this reporting period, including a public consultation on the environmental impact assessment of the plan to produce nickel ore in Blocks 2 and 3 in Bahodopi, according to Government Regulation No. 22/2021 on Environmental Protection and Management. Stakeholders from the district government of Morowali in Central Sulawesi and representatives from the Ministry of Environment and Forestry and the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources attended the public consultation.

Despite the decrease in nickel production, the Company was able to optimize the economic value generated from nickel in matte sales to U\$1,179,452 thousand, growing 23.7% from 2021 which reached US\$953,174 thousand. This achievement was also supported by a commitment to managing ESG during 2022, which was carried out among others through energy efficiency, implementation of occupational safety and health (OSH), and regulatory compliance. PT Vale also supports transparency and Indonesia's EITI reporting. Moreover, during the reporting period, PT Vale contributed US\$179,020 thousand in tax and non-tax state revenue payments to the state, a 58% increase from US\$113,080 thousand in 2021.
#### Dear stakeholders,

Our adoption of ISO 31000:2018, ISO 55001:2014, and COSO-ERM on Risk and Asset Management in managing risks contributed to the achievement of PT Vale's sustainability performance in 2022. One of our focuses in sustainability risk management is climate change, which we manage by referring to the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosure (TCFD). We set a Roadmap Towards Carbon Neutral 2050, with energy efficiency and optimized use of renewable energy as the short-term target, 33% absolute emission reductions from scopes 1 and 2 as the mid-term target for 2030, and carbon neutral (net zero emission) as the long-term target for 2050 or 10 years earlier than Indonesia's target.

PT Vale always involves the community in managing the risks of all activities that we will carry out. We should be grateful because no work was delayed due to rejection from the community or other non-technical factors in 2022. It confirms that PT Vale carried out all operational activities responsibly and by considering the community. In this reporting period, the Company realized cooperation in constructing a ferronickel processing plant in Bahodopi, a High-Pressure Acid Leaching (HPAL) facility Pomalaa and Sorowako.

The HPAL projects have provided us with opportunities to improve our contribution to the joint effort to reduce GHG emissions. The plant and facilities were built using eco-friendly technology by gradually using liquefied natural gas (LNG) for power generation to supply energy to reduction furnaces, making them low emissions. In a projection prepared by an expert team, the ferronickel processing facility in Bahodopi will be Indonesia's second plant with the lowest emission intensity in 2030 after the nickel-in-matte processing plant in Sorowako with an estimated 38 tCO2 e/tNi. Additionally, the carbon emission intensity of the HPAL facility. Another contribution comes from processed nickel products from each processing facility, which will be a vital commodity in the energy transition, particularly in building renewable infrastructure and supporting electrification through electric vehicles. Increased demand for nickel will lead to PT Vale's positive financial performance in the coming years.

Indeed, we are aware that our commitment to implementing best practices faces external local, national, and global dynamics. One of them is the various standards for sustainability performance evaluation and initiatives to support ESG management. We are responding to it by trying to gradually comply with the

various standards – including the International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM), ISO 26000, and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) – and the existing initiatives while still taking into account our investors' needs. In 2022 PT Vale has conducted an ESG gap assessment and prepared a 5 year roadmap based on these standards. We ensure that our investors have comprehensive information about PT Vale's sustainability practices.

Concluding this message, we would like to thank all stakeholders for supporting PT Vale's sustainability practices. We hope that the support will continue and the established cooperation will be better to lead us in realizing our ambition to pioneer sustainable mining practices in Indonesia and even the world.

## **Sustainability Governance Structure**

Our sustainability governance refers to good corporate governance (GCG). The governance organization structure follows Law No. 40 of 2007 on Limited Liability Companies, consisting of the General Meeting of Shareholders as the highest governance unit, the Board of Directors as the unit that manages the Company, and the Board of Commissioners as a supervisor assisted by committees. The nomination and appointment of directors and commissioners are the shareholders' authority, ratified in the General Meeting of Shareholders. We guarantee no conflicts of interest between the Board of Directors, the Board of Commissioners, and the shareholders that can affect the decisions made. This information has been disclosed in the 2022 Annual Report of PT Vale Indonesia Tbk. **[2-9a][2-9b][2-9c][2-10a][2-10b][2-15a][2-15b]**

Sustainability governance implementation is the collective responsibility of the directors, under the coordination of the President Director, who is also the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) as the highestranking officer of sustainability governance. The directors implement sustainability governance based on Vale's 2030 Commitment, structured as key performance indicators covering the economic, environmental, social, and governance aspects. KPI achievement is evaluated regularly and reported to shareholders. **[POJK51-E.1] [2-11a][2-11b][2-12a][2-12b] [2-12c]**

The directors may delegate authority to implement sustainability governance to a company official according to his/her scope of responsibilities. To fulfill corporate social responsibility (CSR), the directors may delegate authority to the External Relation and

Remuneration for commissioners and directors is specifically decided by shareholders through the General Meeting of Shareholders, taking into account the Company's performance, including its sustainability management. Shareholders are the only stakeholders involved in the commissioner and director remuneration decision-making. #### **Product Safety and Impact Management [POJK51-F.27] [POJK51-F.28]**

PT Vale's nickel in matte production and the products comply with the Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) standards and ISO 17025:2008 certification. Nickel in matte is an intermediate product used as a raw material in further processing by buyers without directly impacting the buyers or the environment. The Company never received any complaints about the impacts of the products on employees', workers' and buyers' health and safety during the reporting period. **[416-1a] [416-2a][416-2b]**
### **Product Withdrawals and Customer Satisfaction [POJK51-F.29] [POJK51-F.30]**

No products were withdrawn at buyers' request in 2022. Nickel in matte is transported to buyers in a 3.3-ton special package. Information labels on origin, product specifications, and handling instructions are affixed outside the package. PT Vale evaluated all its products to see their compliance with labelling procedures. There were never any complaints from buyers about information discrepancies on the labels. We were never fined or legally sanctioned for alleged non-compliance with marketing communication regulations. **[417-1a][417-1b][417-2a] [417-2b][417-3a][417-3c]**

We always maintain the quality of products and services to buyers. PT Vale's customers have a long-term contracts, therefore there is no customer satisfaction survey. However, PT Vale and customers routinely hold monthly meetings regarding the performance and if problems found they will be followed up at these meetings.

We ensure that the data of buyers is stored safely. We use a security system to protect data from corruption, modification, and unauthorized dissemination.
